Added mark_applied() tracking (tags_applied_at/collection_applied_at/summary_applied_at) so the digest stops suggesting things already pushed -- resolves the open design question in favor of tracking. Escaped all dynamic content (item titles, error messages, source names, collection titles, tags, config paths) via rich.markup.escape() since titles/collections come from arbitrary web content and Raindrop collections that can contain literal brackets -- verified this explicitly with a bracket/angle-bracket-laden title through mark and apply, nothing broke. digest.py/cmd_digest untouched (that's e5b.3). digest --print now renders through rich.markdown.Markdown instead of dumping raw source; saved digest-YYYY-MM-DD.md/latest.md files are unaffected (same build_digest() output, just rendered differently at print time). Added a rich.progress bar around the stale-item loop, gated by the same needs_fresh check that already controls collection-name fetching -- no bar shown on a fully-cached digest.

Along the way, fixed a real markdown-structure bug this surfaced: <sub> tags and lazy blockquote continuation (no '>' prefix on the Action line) were causing Summary/Action/suggestion/key to merge into one garbled paragraph under any real CommonMark renderer -- previously invisible because --print just dumped raw markdown source. Restructured each stale/aging/new item into properly blank-line-separated blocks (bullet header, blockquote, suggestion line, key line, each as *emphasis* instead of raw <sub> HTML) and collapsed Summary+Action onto one line to avoid blockquote soft-break ambiguity. This fixes both the new --print rendering and the previously-broken structure of the saved .md files themselves. Verified: rendered output structure, raw saved file structure, piped/non-TTY --print (clean degradation, single-line progress bar summary, no ANSI codes), and full command regression.

Added _is_interactive() (sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()) gate in _find_single_item(). When both are true and there's an ambiguous match, uses questionary.select() to let the user pick interactively; a cancelled picker (Ctrl-C/Esc, .ask() returns None) is treated the same as no match. Non-interactive contexts (cron, scripts, piped, and this sandboxed environment itself) keep the exact old behavior: print the list, return None, exit 1 -- verified against a real subprocess with no attached tty, plus mocked-isatty tests for the select/cancel/unambiguous-skips-picker paths. Full command regression unaffected.

Added a 'CLI Experience' section covering rich-formatted output, digest --print Markdown rendering (saved files unaffected), the progress bar's fully-cached-skips-it behavior, and the questionary interactive picker's TTY-only gating. Added 'unhoard synthesize <key> [--force]'. Fetches full article text via summarize.py's existing fetch_article_text() (same trafilatura path already used for AI summaries) and writes a standalone note to <output_dir>/synthesized/<slug>.md with YAML frontmatter (title/url/source/key/tags/synthesized_at) plus a Summary section (if a cached AI summary exists) and the full text. Frontmatter strings/arrays are built with json.dumps(), which produces valid YAML flow scalars/sequences -- verified round-tripping a title with brackets, colons, and quotes through a real YAML parser. Won't overwrite an existing note unless --force is passed (real file-existence check, not just the new synthesized_at DB column, which is informational only). Empty/unfetchable article text fails cleanly with exit 1 instead of writing a useless note. Distinct from mark --unhoarded, which stays a separate, later step.

Gotcha worth recording for future CLI tests here: unhoard.ui's `console`/`err_console` Console singletons detect color support and terminal width once at import time -- before pytest's capsys has redirected stdout/stderr for any given test -- so captured output keeps ANSI escape codes and gets Rich's terminal-width line-wrapping regardless of what capsys does later. Plain `"foo" in captured.out` assertions break both on embedded escape codes and on long messages getting a real newline injected mid-phrase. Fixed by locally overriding the `capsys` fixture in test_cli.py to strip ANSI codes and collapse whitespace before returning `.out`/`.err`, so every other test in the file can assert on captured text normally.

All commands invoked via cli_module.main(argv) (real argparse parsing), not by hand-building argparse.Namespace, so subparser wiring/defaults are exercised too. Seeding/inspection uses a local `store` fixture opened at cfg.state_db_path -- the same path cmd_* resolves via their own internal load_config() call -- so pre-seeded rows and post-command assertions are visible across the separate StateStore connections each side opens.
